article: Culture is all of our business
stem: Senior management requests advice from a chief compliance officer regarding staff surveys indicating reluctance to raise concerns despite strong policy-completion figures. Which course of action is MOST defensible?
options: Test speak-up and leadership behaviors, address local barriers, but defer tracking whether employee experience improves until after management considers the matter closed.
Assume a high helpline volume proves employees feel safe reporting.
Delegate cultural assessment to corporate communications without compliance involvement.
Test speak-up and leadership behaviors, address local barriers, and track whether employee experience improves.
explanation: The best choice is to test speak-up and leadership behaviors, address local barriers, and track whether employee experience improves. This approach focuses on ethical culture rather than relying on an untested shortcut. The other options either substitute assertions for evidence, postpone assessment, or weaken accountability. Editorial basis: CEP 2026-05, Culture is all of our business, p. 20; verify the precise article passage before using this in a scored mock exam.
